edges.qualification: Documents specific transmission channels, not a single origin or uptake effect.

scope.configuration: Named early eighteenth-century testimony and practitioner contacts.

edges.dispute: Elite correspondence mediates and may distort practitioners' contributions.

edges.qualification: Instruction and legitimacy were part of the programme; separate effect not identified.

scope.configuration: Ottoman free-provision and instructional programme from the 1840s.

alternatives: Local trusted practitioners without equivalent imperial publications
edges.dispute: Official intentions do not reveal recipient belief change.

edges.qualification: Resources supported delivery; the exact bundle is not a timeless vaccination prerequisite.

scope.configuration: Ottoman professional vaccination provision, including rural access.

alternatives: Imported vaccine rather than local production
edges.dispute: Rural refusals, instability and resource shortfalls cannot be ranked separately.

edges.qualification: Rules created administrative pressure for institutional uptake; actual enforcement effects unknown.

scope.configuration: 1885–1915 certification linked to school, service and other obligations.

edges.dispute: Legal leverage is documented; consent, coverage and welfare are not implied.

edges.qualification: Registration accompanied expanded vaccination obligations.

scope.configuration: Late Ottoman newborn, vaccination and certification records.

edges.dispute: Intended registration coverage exceeded demonstrated administrative reach.

edges.qualification: Identified teaching channels supported reproduction of practice.

scope.configuration: Listerian operations and dressing routines in British professional networks.

edges.dispute: Motivated trainee selection and prestige could contribute to observed uptake.

edges.qualification: Outcome records participated in evaluation and contestation; they did not supply unambiguous proof.

scope.configuration: British comparison of defined procedures and ward outcomes, 1867–1890.

alternatives: Case narratives and direct clinical observation
edges.dispute: Small counts, selection, epidemic cycles and changing procedures make early causal interpretation contested.

edges.qualification: Estimated joint health contribution is scoped to the Massachusetts configuration.

scope.configuration: Protected water and effective sewerage in the regional study.

edges.dispute: Complementarity varies with disease environment and efficiency; not universal joint necessity.

edges.qualification: Mandated participation/payment was the observed coordination route.

scope.configuration: Regional sewerage to address cross-jurisdiction pollution.

edges.dispute: No identified comparison proves this coercive route uniquely necessary or distributionally benign.

edges.qualification: Submerged fermentation was one realized large-scale supply route.

scope.configuration: Pfizer penicillin production during 1941–1945.

edges.dispute: Commemorative account lacks primary comparative batch records.

edges.qualification: Media/strain work and processing supported usable output, rather than tanks alone.

scope.configuration: Specified US wartime production process.

alternatives: Different strains, media or downstream processing routes
edges.dispute: Relative causal contribution and transfer across companies not quantified.

edges.qualification: Coordination accompanied risky production expansion.

scope.configuration: Public-laboratory/company cooperation and wartime industrial commitment.

alternatives: Private investment without the same public coordination
edges.dispute: Counterfactual finance and procurement effects unresolved.

edges.qualification: Account identifies concrete prior technical capability applied to penicillin.

scope.configuration: Pfizer deep-tank experience carried from gluconic acid to penicillin.

edges.dispute: Company-centred retrospective; not a cross-firm matched comparison.

edges.qualification: Spraying was part of suppression, not a standalone guarantee.

scope.configuration: Sri Lankan postwar vector-control programme with treatment/surveillance.

edges.dispute: Counts and operational chronology do not identify the chemical's independent effect.

edges.qualification: Field capacity and case detection/treatment accompanied early suppression; later elimination is a distinct configuration.

scope.configuration: Early Sri Lankan suppression with case detection and treatment accompanying spraying.

edges.dispute: Official retrospective causal emphasis and shared programme data; no single fixed bundle across all decades.

edges.qualification: Relaxation precedes resurgence, supporting an operational account without allocating sole causation.

scope.configuration: Withdrawal/reduction of control with residual transmission potential.

edges.dispute: Migration, ecology, undetected resistance and measurement changes may interact.

edges.qualification: Replacement is a dated Sri Lankan insecticide episode, not global DDT abandonment.

scope.configuration: Malathion replaced DDT for indoor residual spraying in the cited account.

alternatives: Other insecticides or nonchemical vector measures
edges.dispute: Replacement timing is reported; all comparative efficacy and acceptance outcomes not audited.

edges.qualification: Demonstration/monitoring were observed implementation activities; net campaign effect not isolated.

scope.configuration: BRAC practical teaching in covered villages.

edges.dispute: Knowledge tests and reported use differ; programme-affiliated evaluation.

edges.qualification: Distribution widened delivery options while home preparation continued.

scope.configuration: Packaged ORS in the sampled programme villages and retail network.

edges.dispute: Broad survey ORT definition does not equate to correct packaged formulation use.

edges.qualification: Family administration demonstrated practical delivery under emergency staffing constraints.

scope.configuration: Refugee camps at the India–Bangladesh border.

edges.dispute: Historical participant accounts; no universal substitution for medical supervision inferred.

edges.qualification: Financial interpretation supported by randomized scripts and rival-signal tests.

scope.configuration: Mild-symptom young standardized patients in one city.

alternatives: Prescribing decisions under other remuneration systems
edges.dispute: Expected revenue is partly bundled with social/quality signals; broader reform effects unknown.

edges.qualification: Demand raised prescribing when hospital dispensing was expected; effect strongly conditional.

scope.configuration: Explicit patient requests under specified purchase-location scripts.

edges.dispute: Interaction does not mean both inputs are necessary: baseline prescribing was already high.

edges.qualification: Randomized outside-purchase script sharply reduced prescriptions in this sample.

scope.configuration: Standardized mild-illness encounters, not a system-wide financing reform.

edges.dispute: Effect of script identified more strongly than its exclusive financial mechanism.

edges.qualification: Packaged and home-prepared options coexisted; their relative use changed.

scope.configuration: Sampled Bangladesh villages with packet availability and home preparation knowledge.

alternatives: Both may remain in use for different episodes
edges.dispute: No causal product-switching estimate; availability, convenience and preferences intertwined.
